Corrosion Verification: During the experimental testing, 6 corrosion coupons (three SS-316L and three SS- 304L) were located inside sulfur TES lab prototype to verify if the corrosion rate profile matches the trends obtained from corrosion testing conducted in Task 3. Figure 33 shows the temperature measured by the internal thermocouples near the placement of the corrosion coupons. Overall, the coupons were exposed to hot molten sulfur at an average temperature of 206.4 oC for a time duration of 984 hours. Figure 33 also shows the photograph of the corrosion coupons that were cleaned after the corrosion testing. The plot in Figure 34 shows the calculated corrosion rates based on weight loss measurement. The corrosion rate per year was obtained was obtained based on linear extrapolation as follows: CR [microns/year] = (A×8760)/984 where A is the metal loss thickness in microns. As observed from Fig. 34, the corrosion rates of SS316L and SS304L coupons ranged from 1.1 to 1.7 micron per year. This is lower than the corrosion rate of 25-35 microns per year measured in Task 3. The primary reason is that the coupons inside the lab prototype unit were exposed to a lower temperature (206 oC) compared to the 300 oC exposure in Task 3. Interestingly, the measured rates are closer to the 2 micron per year corrosion rate predicted for SS-316L using the parabolic rate law discussed in Task 3. Overall, the results in Figure 34 indicate that the corrosion rates are much less than the values measured from isothermal testing in Task 3 and the target threshold of 50 microns per year.
